title: Bail, Anticipatory Bail and Custody Rules
content: Section 496 CrPC: In bailable offences, bail is an absolute right upon furnishing bail bond. Section 497 CrPC: In non-bailable offences, bail is discretionary; court may release minors under 16, women, sick or infirm. Section 498 CrPC: High Court Division and Court of Session have extraordinary jurisdiction to grant anticipatory bail prior to arrest.

title: Dishonour of Cheque for Insufficiency of Funds
content: Section 138 NI Act: Offence committed if cheque returned unpaid due to insufficient funds. Punishment: Up to 1 year imprisonment or fine up to 3 times the cheque amount or both. Mandatory procedure: Cheque presented within 6 months; written legal notice within 30 days of dishonour memo; drawer given 30 days to pay; formal criminal complaint filed within 30 days after notice period expiry.

act: The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 & Police Act, 1861
title: First Information Report (FIR) vs General Diary (GD)
content: Section 154 CrPC: Cognizable offence information must be recorded as FIR (Form 27). Police can investigate and arrest without magistrate warrant. Section 155 CrPC & Police Act Section 44: Non-cognizable matters, lost documents, or prospective threats are entered into General Diary (GD). Police cannot investigate GD without judicial order under Section 155(2).
source: Laws of Bangladesh & Master Legal Document (/Allfile.pdf)

act: The Specific Relief Act, 1877 & Land Crime Prevention and Redress Act, 2023
act_bn: সুনির্দিষ্ট প্রতিকার আইন, ১৮৭৭ ও ভূমি অপরাধ প্রতিরোধ ও প্রতিকার আইন, ২০২৩
title: Dispossession, Illegal Land Grabbing and Title Declaration
content: Section 9 Specific Relief Act 1877: Summary suit for recovery of possession within 6 months of illegal dispossession without proof of title. Section 8: Recovery based on proven proprietary title. Land Crime Act 2023: Illegal occupancy, forged deeds punishable with up to 7 years imprisonment. State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 Section 143: e-Mutation at AC Land office required to update revenue record.
source: Laws of Bangladesh & Ministry of Land (land.gov.bd)

act: Cyber Security Ordinance, 2025 (Ordinance No. 25 of 2025), which repealed the Cyber Security Act, 2023; and the Pornography Control Act, 2012
act_bn: সাইবার নিরাপত্তা অধ্যাদেশ, ২০২৫ (সাইবার নিরাপত্তা আইন, ২০২৩ রহিতকারী) ও পর্নোগ্রাফি নিয়ন্ত্রণ আইন, ২০১২
title: Online Harassment, Blackmail, Account Hijacking and Impersonation
content: The Cyber Security Act, 2023 (Act No. 46 of 2023) was repealed on 21 May 2025 by the Cyber Security Ordinance, 2025 (Ordinance No. 25 of 2025). Do NOT cite sections 24 or 25 of the 2023 Act as current law: press reports on the Ordinance say sections 21, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 31 and 34 of the 2023 Act were omitted, while sections 17, 18, 19, 20, 22, 23, 30, 32 and 35 were carried over. Section numbers in the Ordinance itself must be checked against the official gazette text before being cited. Online harassment, hacking, impersonation and blackmail using intimate images remain reportable to the police (national emergency number 999) and are prosecuted under the cyber ordinance, the Pornography Control Act 2012 and the Penal Code 1860 (extortion, cheating by personation, criminal intimidation). Victims should preserve screenshots, profile URLs and timestamps before reporting.
source: Press reports: Prothom Alo, Observer BD, Views Bangladesh (May 2025); confirm against bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd

title: Mandatory Tax Return Filing, e-TIN and Tax Day
content: Section 166: Mandatory annual tax return submission for all e-TIN holders and taxable individuals. Section 171: November 30 designated as Tax Day for individual taxpayers. Section 174 & 266: Penalties and 2% monthly delay interest for filing past Tax Day. Section 264: Proof of submission required across 43+ civic and financial services.
source: Laws of Bangladesh & National Board of Revenue (etaxnbr.gov.bd)

act: The Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, 1972
title: Fundamental Rights and Writ Jurisdiction
content: Part III (Articles 26-47A): Equality before law (Art 27), right to protection of law (Art 31), right to life and liberty (Art 32), safeguards upon arrest (Art 33), freedom of speech (Art 39). Article 102: Power of High Court Division to issue Writs of Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Certiorari, Prohibition and Quo Warranto.

act: The Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 & The Family Courts Ordinance, 1985
act_bn: মুসলিম পারিবারিক আইন অধ্যাদেশ, ১৯৬১ ও পারিবারিক আদালত অধ্যাদেশ, ১৯৮৫
title: Dower (Mahr), Talaq Notice, Maintenance and Polygamy
content: Section 10 MFLO: Dower is prompt (payable on demand) unless expressly deferred in Kabinnama. Section 7 MFLO: Mandatory written notice to Chairman and spouse; Talaq not effective until 90 days elapse. Section 6: Second marriage without Arbitration Council permission is punishable offense. Family Courts Ordinance 1985: Family Courts have exclusive jurisdiction for dower, maintenance, restitution of conjugal rights and custody.
source: Laws of Bangladesh & Master Legal Reference (/Allfile.pdf)
